subject: Immediate: Late-hour memory-alignment shim applied — action for long-context jobs
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <jenna@nimbleapps.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-17T23:12:00-07:00
Subject: Immediate: Late-hour memory-alignment shim applied — action for long-context jobs

Hi Jenna —

Quick note: at 23:05 PST we rolled a short-lived memory-alignment shim to address an emergent alignment mismatch observed on quantized kernels when serving requests with very long contexts (>12k tokens). The shim is in place now; it reduces the chance of token truncation and invalid outputs but can cause short-lived 502/stream truncation for in-flight requests while connections drain.

What to expect now:
- Most requests should complete normally; a small percentage of long-context calls may return truncated output or a transient 502 for 10–90s while state is reconciled.
- If you see truncated responses, please retry the request once; we recommend temporarily lowering sequence length for batched/long-running jobs until we issue the follow-up patch tomorrow.

Attachments: memory_shim_patch_notes.pdf (shortnotes) and patch-deploy-log.txt (deploy record).

We apologize for the late-hour notice — we took the decision because we were seeing corruption risk under specific long-context workloads. If you want us to proactively pause the jobs you mentioned earlier, let us know and we can schedule a controlled restart.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-17T23:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: Late-hour memory-alignment shim applied — action for long-context jobs

Vanessa / team —

Quick engineering note for the record: root cause appears to be an alignment edge in the quantized attention kernels that manifests for sequences exceeding ~12k tokens on certain precompiled kernels (observed on both A100 and H100 pools running the 8-bit quant builds). The shim adds a conservative alignment guard that prevents a small class of OOB writes during prefix extension.

Operationally:
- We applied the shim to the affected rollout group at 23:05 PST. No service-wide restart was required but in-flight KV state for some sessions was reconciled, which led to brief truncation for those requests.
- We rolled additional telemetry (INF-4521) to track post-shim token-accuracy deltas and will push a targeted kernel recompile tomorrow morning with a full revert path.

Immediate ask for CS: advise customers to retry once; if they report persistent failures, create a support ticket with the sample request + job id and we’ll priority debug.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
SRE — Inference Runtime

From: Jenna Park <jenna@nimbleapps.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@nimbleapps.com
Date: 2028-01-17T23:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: Late-hour memory-alignment shim applied — action for long-context jobs

Thanks for the heads up, Vanessa.

We saw the behavior on two of our nightly batch jobs that stream documents into a long-context summarization flow. One of the jobs returned a truncated summary (attached screenshot). Most jobs recovered after a retry. A couple of older jobs still show partial outputs in our logs.

Can you confirm whether the shim will affect inference latency for our batch runs? Also — if you need sample request IDs or payloads, I can send 3 examples now.

Appreciate the quick response.

— Jenna
VP of Product, NimbleApps

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <jenna@nimbleapps.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-18T00:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: Late-hour memory-alignment shim applied — action for long-context jobs

Jenna —

Thanks for sending that. The screenshot helps. Short answers:
- Latency: the shim adds negligible per-token overhead; you should not see meaningful increases for single requests. Some batched long-context jobs may see a 2–6% tail increase while KV reconciliation runs, but we expect that to normalize.
- Persistent partial outputs: please send the three sample request IDs and the payloads. We’ll correlate with the deploy log and reprocess them in a safe sandbox.

Temporary mitigations you can apply immediately (no code change except headers/params):
1) Add header X-Redwood-Fallback: true to force the non-quantized fallback variant for long jobs.
2) If you submit via the SDK, set ?variant=stable (this pins the model to the non-quant path).
3) Requeue affected jobs with a slightly reduced max_context (e.g., 12k -> 10k) if possible for tonight’s batch window.

We will schedule a kernel recompile and full regression test tomorrow morning (INF-4521). I’ve included the raw deploy log here: https://drive.redwood.com/patches/memory-shim-v1 and the short notes in the attachment.

Rishi Malhotra
Engineering Lead, Runtime

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <jenna@nimbleapps.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-18T01:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: Late-hour memory-alignment shim applied — action for long-context jobs

Hi Jenna —

Thanks — we’ll take the three sample request IDs when you’re ready and prioritize reprocessing. For clarity on next steps:
- Short term: follow Rishi’s mitigation steps (header/variant) if you can. We’ll also requeue the two affected jobs on our side if you prefer — just tell us which job ids.
- Tomorrow: engineering will push a kernel recompile and full regression across our quant variants; we’ll publish a full postmortem and timeline and follow up with a short remediation call.

Proposed follow-up: 11:00 AM PST tomorrow for a 30-min sync to review the postmortem and confirm remediation. Does that work for your team?

Again, apologies for the late hour — we pushed the shim to avoid a higher-probability corruption mode.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-18T02:09:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: INF-4521 follow-up and action items

Internal summary:
- Event: emergent alignment mismatch on quant kernels for >12k token contexts. Shim applied 23:05 PST to prevent OOB writes; caused transient truncations for some in-flight sessions.
- Customer impact: NimbleApps reported 2–3 truncated batch outputs; most recovered after single retry.

Action items (owners):
- Rishi: full kernel recompile + regression by 09:00 PST tomorrow; include cross-hardware validation (H100 + A100). (owner: rishi)
- Stephanie: expand telemetry alerting for token-accuracy delta and add automatic roll-back trigger if delta > 0.5% across production traffic. (owner: stephanie)
- Vanessa: coordinate 11:00 AM PST customer sync and gather sample request IDs from Jenna. (owner: vanessa)
- Connor: prepare an internal runbook for how to safely reprocess affected jobs and capture deterministic inputs for debugging. (owner: connor)

I also created the INF ticket and linked the deploy artifacts here: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4521. We will publish a customer-facing postmortem doc to https://docs.redwood.com/postmortems/INF-4521-memory-shim when ready.

— Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Operations
